text:
Sam: Heads up — probebench shows a perf regression on sm92 for INT4/FP8 after the kernel-handoff tweak. +12% p99 at seq=2048, batch=1. Repro steps below, can someone triage?

Maria: Seen this too. Repro locally on hopper. Looks like a KV cache pressure + kernel pick flip to fp8_gemm_v2 around mid-layers.

Arjun: Can you paste the probebench trace/logs? any cuda mem warnings or alloc spikes?

Sam: Repro snippet + relevant trace lines:
```
./probebench --model llama-70b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --quant int4fp8 --arch sm92 --kernels=autotune
# trace excerpt:
kernel_pick: fp8_gemm_v2 chosen at layer 14
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.28
scratch_allocs(layer20): 12
latency_total_ms: 1234 -> 1380
```

Chen: My hunch: the autotuner's cost curve prefers fp8_gemm_v2 for mem/cost, but on sm92 long sequences it causes extra temporary scratch allocations + memcpy churn (maybe workspace alignment differences). That explains the jump in p99. We need a per-arch safety margin or a seq-length cutoff.

Maria: Agreed. Short-term mitigations: 1) log more metadata on kernel picks (seq, kv-residency, scratch bytes), 2) gate fp8 handoff for sm92 when seq > 1536, or 3) increase hysteresis so we don't flip mid-session.

Sam: Also saw this in dmesg/gpu logs: GPU memory fragmentation warnings and occasional cuMemPoolAlloc timeout near layer 20. Makes sense if scratch gets bigger for fp8 kernel.

Leo: I can push a quick override: set per-arch preference map: {"sm92": {"prefer_quant": "int8", "seq_threshold": 1536, "hysteresis_ms": 80}} for canary. Will run probebench across the failing cases.

devbot: deploy-bot: feature flag "quant-pick-sm92-handoff" enabled in canary.

Arjun: Upload a full CUPTI/nvprof trace to S3 pls so we can compare kernel timings + memcpy hotspots. Also capture KV cache hit/miss timeline.

Sam: Uploaded: https://s3.redwood/artifacts/2087654321/trace.tar.gz — includes cupTI, probebench logs, and kernel pick debug. Initial canary (with Leo's override) brought p99 back to baseline on a few runs. Need more matrix runs.

Maria: I'll add a regression matrix: seq=[512,1024,1536,2048], batch=[1,4,8], arch=[sm86,sm92,sm99], quant=[int4,int8,fp8]. Script + collect traces. Also add microbench for memcpy & scratch_alloc counts per kernel pick.

Arjun: Suggest autotuner ingest metrics: scratch_allocs, memcpy_bytes, kv_cache_residency to compute a long-seq penalty term. Could be a simple additive cost for seq>threshold per-arch.

Chen: Yep. We should also record 'fallback_count' when kernel fails and needs to swap, so the orchestrator can punish aggressive picks.

Sam: I'll open a PR with (1) extra kernel-pick logging, (2) per-arch override flag, (3) canary config. Tagging @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup: 

Maria: Good. After the automated sweep, let's reconvene and decide permanent autotuner rule (hysteresis vs cost-term).

Arjun: If Leo's canary stays green, we can roll to dedicated and monitor the cost delta. Also add an alert if p99 regresses >5% for 30m post-rollout.

Sam: Thanks all — plan is: Leo push canary, Maria run matrix, Arjun add perf ingestion proposal, Chen add fallback metrics. I'll follow up with PR link.
